newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel invests S$50 mln on multimedia.
newsitem.headline: SingTel invests S$50 mln on multimedia.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) expects to invest up to Singapore $50 million on new multimedia services by end of this year, serion official Paul Chong said on Tuesday.
Chong, assistant vice president of consumer services, told a news conference the investment could be higher depending on the number of subscribers that SingTel gets for the service.
He declined to give revenue projections for SingTel's multimedia service, Magix, launched last week at the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair in Signapore.
Magix offers a wide range of text, video and on-line services via the customers' personal computers.
When SingTel's ADSL (asymmetrical digital subscriber line) high speed broadband network goes nationwide by October, all SingTel subscribers will be able to get the services, Chong said.
He expected most of the revenue from Magix to be generated from its video on demand and fast Internet services.
SingTel will be charging a one-time registration fee of S$30 and a monthly subscription charge of S$25 for Magix. In addition, there is an access charge of S$0.05 cents per minute (or S$3 an hour).
